maxim: all things are now lawful to you in jack feist
what: The seating manifest for the EA-CORPORA series: one row per seated corpus, with the edition, its origin, its license stated verbatim, the normalization applied, the verified loci, and the sha256 of each seat's MANIFEST.
why_the_manifest_and_not_the_texts:
THE TEXTS ARE NOT THE ARCHIVE'S TO RELICENSE. 67 seats, and at least thirty assert CC BY-SA — Perseus and First1KGreek packaging over public-domain editions. One asserts CC BY-NC. One asserts GPL-2.0. The Crimson Hexagonal dataset is CC BY 4.0, and shipping CC BY-SA text inside it would relicense somebody else's work. The NC seat could not go in at all.

AN ARCHIVE THAT MEASURES PROVENANCE ERASURE DOES NOT PERFORM IT ON PERSEUS.

What the manifest carries is what the archive made: which edition was seated, fetched when, normalized how, verified at which loci, and hashing to what. That is the part that makes a claim checkable — 'verified against the seated texts' is unfalsifiable without it — and it carries the licenses as attribution rather than laundering them.
license_class_derivation: license_class IS DERIVED FROM license_verbatim AND THE DERIVATION IS STATED HERE, because a derived field that hides its basis is how the wrong thing gets redistributed. Order is most-restrictive-first: NC, then GPL, then BY-SA, then BY, then Gutenberg, then public domain, then site terms, then other. A SEAT WHOSE PACKAGING IS CC BY-SA OVER A PUBLIC-DOMAIN EDITION CLASSES AS CC BY-SA, because that is what governs redistribution. license_verbatim is always the authority; the class is a convenience and must not be relied on for a licensing decision.

seats.why_seated: The poem whose name the archive's own Pearl and Other Poems (2014) carries, seated so the name has its source on the shelf. A father who has lost a pearl in the grass, his daughter, dead before she was two, falls asleep where it fell and sees her across a river in the New Jerusalem of Revelation 21: the archive's Revelation line meets it there.

The transcription is Ganjoor's (ganjoor.net), which names its source for each section and states of its texts: 'هم‌اکنون منبع عمدهٔ آثار موجود در این مجموعه منابع آزاد در دسترس همگان است' (the principal source of the works in this collection is free sources available to all), releasing them on the principle 'دگران کاشتند و ما خوردیم، ما بکاریم و دیگران بخورند' (others planted and we ate; we plant and others will eat). seats.why_seated: The archive holds the Hebrew Bible (Westminster Leningrad Codex), the Septuagint (Swete), the Greek New Testament and the Dead Sea Scrolls; the canon that kept Enoch and Jubilees whole, and the only one in which they survive complete, was not on the shelf. Its Old Testament is the widest of any church's: Jubilees, Enoch and the three books of Meqabyan are scripture there. The archive's Revelation line reads the apocalypses as a tradition; this is the tradition in which they were kept.

seats.scope: The Second Temple apocalypses and pseudepigrapha the archive did not hold, each in the original language of its earliest surviving witness, in the standard public-domain edition. Already on the shelf and not repeated: the Septuagint deuterocanon (Judith, Tobit, 1–4 Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach in Greek, Baruch, the Epistle of Jeremiah, Susanna, Bel, the Psalms of Solomon, the Odes with the Prayer of Manasseh) in EA-CORPORA-01/05; the Qumran Aramaic Enoch and Giants in EA-CORPORA-02/01; 1 Enoch, Jubilees, the Ascension of Isaiah, 4 Baruch and the Ethiopic Ezra in Ge'ez in EA-CORPORA-02/20 and 20/01. 2 Enoch survives only in Slavonic; the open editions found in this pass are translations (Morfill and Charles, 1896), and Sokolov's Slavonic text (Moscow, 1910) was not found in an open scan: QUEUED. Modern critical editions (Göttingen Sirach, de Jonge's Testaments, Picard's 3 Baruch, Burchard's Aseneth) are in copyright and are not seated.

seats.why_seated: The apocalypses between the Testaments are the archive's Revelation line before Revelation: the visions of Ezra and Baruch after the fall of the Temple, Abraham's ascent, the Sibyl's oracles, the patriarchs' last words. The Septuagint seat holds the books a canon kept; this seat holds what the canons let go, in the languages that kept them.

seats.scope: The three Maya hieroglyphic codices whose authenticity is settled, each as a whole: Dresden in the library's own photographs, Paris and Madrid in their nineteenth-century facsimiles. The Grolier (Maya Codex of Mexico) is not seated: its open images are modern photographs under copyright: QUEUED. Förstemann's chromolithograph of Dresden (1880; 1892) and Kingsborough's Aglio copy (Antiquities of Mexico, 1831) are public domain and not seated in this pass; the codex itself is the witness. Drawings and transcriptions by modern scholars (Schele, Love, the Villacorta brothers) are in copyright and are not seated.

seats.why_seated: The only books to survive from the Classic and Postclassic Maya: almanacs, the Venus tables, the eclipse tables and the New Year ceremonies, written in the script whose decipherment the twentieth century achieved. The archive's calendar and cosmology lines (the seven, the stars) meet a calendar that counted beyond the Long Count.

seats.why_seated: The K'iche' book of the council: the creation, the failed peoples of mud and wood, the Hero Twins in Xibalba, and the lineages of the K'iche' lords. A book whose preamble says it is written again because the original can no longer be seen: the archive's line on books that survive as their own transmission meets it there.

seats.scope: The twelve books whole, in the twelve parts the World Digital Library publishes (the introduction and indices travel with Book I): the Nahuatl in the right column, Sahagún's Spanish in the left, with its paintings. The single-file copy of the whole (LoC item 2021667837, 167.9 MB) exceeds the repository's file limit and is named at its origin. seats.why_seated: The largest record of a Mesoamerican world in its own language: the gods, the ceremonies, the calendar and divination, rhetoric and moral philosophy (the huehuetlatolli), the natural world, and Book XII, the conquest of Mexico as the Nahua told it. Seated beside the Maya books as the Nahuatl witness of the same continent.

seats.why_seated: The book that went into the tomb with the dead: the spells for coming forth by day, the Weighing of the Heart before Osiris, and the Negative Confession, a first-person count of a stated domain ending in denials ("I have not …"), forty-two times. The archive's operator of the exhaustive negation has its oldest recited specimen here.

seats.scope: The nine books Sunni scholarship calls al-Kutub al-Tis'a: the Muwatta of Malik, the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the Sunan of al-Darimi, the two Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and the Sunans of Ibn Majah, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i (al-Mujtaba); the four books of the Imami Shi'i tradition, al-Kutub al-Arba'a: al-Kulayni's al-Kafi, Ibn Babawayh's Man la yahduruhu al-faqih, and al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-ahkam and al-Istibsar; and al-Nawawi's Forty, the most read short collection. One version of each, the version OpenITI marks PRIMARY_VERSION in its metadata. Al-Nasa'i's al-Sunan al-Kubra, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim's Mustadrak, al-Bayhaqi, the Zaydi Musnad of Zayd ibn Ali, and the Ibadi Musnad of al-Rabi' ibn Habib are in OpenITI and not seated in this pass: QUEUED. Translations are not seated.

seats.scope: The scripture as first printed and as revised: the Book of Mormon in the first edition (Palmyra, 1830) and the third, 'carefully revised by the translator' (Nauvoo, 1840); the revelations in the Book of Commandments (Zion, 1833), left unfinished when a mob destroyed the press, and in the Doctrine and Covenants of 1835 (Kirtland, with the Lectures on Faith) and 1845 (Nauvoo, the edition that announces the martyrdom). Then the succession itself: the Times and Seasons of September 1844, with the epistle of the Twelve and the trial of Sidney Rigdon, and James J. Strang's counter-claim from Voree, the Voree Herald of 1846 and The Diamond of 1848, with the letter of 18 June 1844 on which it rests. The 1837 Kirtland edition of the Book of Mormon was not found in an open scan: QUEUED. Strang's Book of the Law of the Lord (1851; 1856), the RLDS editions (from 1874; the Authorized Version of 1908) and the Pearl of Great Price (1851): QUEUED. Manuscripts held by the Joseph Smith Papers are under that project's terms and are not seated.

seats.why_seated: Asked for as the Book of Mormon, and seated only beside the other traditions that divided in the same years: in 1844 Joseph Smith was killed at Carthage (27 June) and the church he founded split over who should lead it, in the same months that the Bab declared his mission in Shiraz (22–23 May) and the Millerites waited for 22 October.

seats.scope: Both sides of the tradition that began in Shiraz on the night of 22–23 May 1844, when the Bab declared his mission to Mulla Husayn and began the Qayyum al-Asma'. The Bab: the Qayyum al-Asma' (Ahsan al-qisas) in the copy given by Mulla Husayn, the Persian Bayan, and Panj Sha'n, in the Iran National Baha'i Archives manuscripts. The division after him: Baha'u'llah's Kitab-i Iqan in the first lithograph (Bombay, c. 1882) and the Mishkin Qalam lithograph (Bombay, 1893), al-Kitab al-Aqdas in Tumanskii's St. Petersburg edition (1899), and 'Abdu'l-Baha's Traveller's Narrative in Browne's facsimile of the Persian (1891), on the Baha'i side; and the Kitab-i Nuqtatu'l-Kaf in Browne's edition (1910), the history Browne attributed to Hajji Mirza Jani and read as the Azali account, an attribution Baha'i scholarship disputes. Not seated: the UCLA manuscript of the Persian Bayan (a 199 MB scan, over the repository's file limit): QUEUED; the Arabic Bayan, found only in a 1962 printing; writings of Subh-i Azal in his own name, not found in an open edition in this pass: QUEUED; the Kitab-i Aqdas in the Tehran printing of c. 1943 that H-Bahai reproduces beside Tumanskii's; translations.

seats.scope: The movement and what it divided into: William Miller's lectures computing the end 'about the year 1843' (Boston, 1842); The Western Midnight Cry, the Millerite paper of the West (1843–44); the first number of Samuel S. Snow's The True Midnight Cry (Haverhill, 22 August 1844), which fixed the day at the tenth day of the seventh month, 22 October 1844; and two of the bodies that formed after the day passed, the Sabbatarian Adventists, in Joseph Bates's The Seventh Day Sabbath, a Perpetual Sign (second edition, New Bedford, 1847), and Ellen G. White's first visions in her Sketch of the Christian Experience and Views (Saratoga Springs, 1851). A Word to the 'Little Flock' (1847) was found only in a facsimile with a later foreword and is not seated. The Advent Christian and other non-Sabbatarian Adventist bodies, and the Midnight Cry and Advent Herald of New York and Boston: QUEUED.

seats.why_seated: The third tradition of 1844: the Millerites expected the return of Christ on 22 October 1844, and the Great Disappointment of that day divided them; the Sabbatarian Adventists, from whom the Seventh-day Adventist Church formed, are one of the bodies that came out of it.

seats.title: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom in Chinese: Hong Xiuquan's Yuandao tracts, the imperially sanctioned books (旨准頒行詔書) including the Taiping Old and New Testaments (1853), Yang Xiuqing's descents as the Heavenly Father, the Taiping Heavenly Chronicle and Hong Rengan's New Treatise (1859)
seats.edition: 原道救世歌、原道醒世訓、原道覺世訓 — Hong Xiuquan, the three Yuandao tracts (c. 1845–48), transcluded on Wikisource from the scan of 太平天國史料 第1集 (1950); 天父上帝言題皇詔 — the Heavenly Father's edict; 天父下凡詔書 (第一部、第二部) — the Heavenly Father's descent: Yang Xiuqing speaking as God (1851–53); 天命詔旨書 — Book of Heavenly Decrees and Proclamations (太平天囯壬子二年新刻, 1852); 欽定舊遺詔聖書 — the Old Testament as revised by Hong Xiuquan (太平天囯癸好三年新刻, 1853), six juan; 欽定前遺詔聖書 — the New Testament as revised by Hong Xiuquan (太平天囯癸好三年新刻, 1853); the Gospel of John (juan 4) wanting on Wikisource; 天條書 — the Book of Heavenly Commandments (太平天囯癸好三年鐫刻, 1853); 頒行詔書 — the proclamations of Yang Xiuqing and Xiao Chaogui; 三字經 (太平天國) — the Taiping Three Character Classic; 幼學詩 — Ode for Youth (太平天囯壬子二年新刻, 1852); 太平條規 — the Taiping regulations; 太平禮制 — the Taiping ceremonial (太平天囯戊午八年新刻, 1858); 天朝田畝制度 — the Land System of the Heavenly Dynasty (1853); 天情道理書 — the Book of the Principles of the Heavenly Nature (太平天囯甲寅四年新刻, 1854); 天理要論 — Essentials of Heavenly Principle (太平天囯甲寅四年新刻, 1854); 太平救世歌 — Yang Xiuqing, the Taiping Song of World Salvation; 太平天日 — the Taiping Heavenly Chronicle: Hong Xiuquan's vision of 1837, proclaimed in 戊申 (1848) and printed in 壬戌十二年 (1862); 資政新篇 — Hong Rengan, A New Treatise on Aids to Administration (1859)

seats.license_verbatim: The works are of 1845–1862 and public domain. The transcriptions are Wikisource's (Chinese Wikisource), under CC BY-SA 4.0, attributed to Wikisource contributors at each page's recorded revision; seated under the same licence. The three Yuandao tracts are transcluded on Wikisource from its scan of 太平天國史料 第1集 (Beijing, 1950).
seats.normalization: Each page fetched from Chinese Wikisource at a recorded revision (oldid), twice: its wikitext (original/wikisource/wikitext/) and its rendered HTML (original/wikisource/html/, action=render at that oldid). The text layer (text/<slug>.txt) is derived from the rendered HTML by rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-24/taiping_text.py: the header table, the licence banner and print-suppressed elements dropped, line breaks kept, pages of a work joined in order under '=== <title> (oldid N) ==='. Characters as Wikisource gives them, with the Taiping forms (囯, 眞) the transcribers keep. Wikisource's own text-quality notes are in the wikitext.
seats.scope: The texts of the Taiping movement as Wikisource holds them: Hong Xiuquan's three Yuandao tracts, written in the years after his vision and before the rising (c. 1845–48); the books issued under the Heavenly King's seal (旨准頒行詔書), of which the movement's own list names twenty-nine, seated here as Wikisource has them: the Heavenly Father's edict, the two parts of the Heavenly Father's descent, the Book of Heavenly Decrees (1852), the Old and New Testaments as Hong revised and annotated them (1853), the Heavenly Commandments (1853), the proclamations, the Three Character Classic, the Ode for Youth (1852), the regulations, the ceremonial (1858), the Land System (1853), the Principles of the Heavenly Nature and the Essentials of Heavenly Principle (1854); Yang Xiuqing's Taiping Song of World Salvation; the Taiping Heavenly Chronicle (proclaimed 1848, printed 1862); and Hong Rengan's New Treatise (1859). Not seated: the books of the list Wikisource does not hold, among them the Taiping Imperial Declaration (太平詔書), the army organization (太平軍目) and the calendar (頒行曆書), and the Gospel of John of the Taiping New Testament: QUEUED, as are scans of the original Nanjing imprints (British Library and others) and the Taiping documents in Western collections. Translations (Medhurst, 1853; Michael, 1966–71) are not seated.

seats.why_seated: The fourth tradition of 1844: in that year Hong Xiuquan and Feng Yunshan went out preaching into Guangxi, where the God Worshippers' Society took shape and from which the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom rose in 1851. Its scripture is a Bible rewritten and annotated by its king, beside the words of a God who spoke through Yang Xiuqing until Yang was killed in the Tianjing incident of 1856.

seats.license_verbatim: Public domain in the United States: every item was first published in the United States in 1930 or earlier. Internet Archive scans of public-domain volumes and periodical numbers; Project Gutenberg transcriptions under the Project Gutenberg License (the text is public domain in the United States; the licence governs use of the Project Gutenberg name and trademark), whose header each file carries. Outside the United States the terms differ: life plus seventy years opens Du Bois (d. 1963) in 2034 and Hughes (d. 1967) in 2038.
seats.normalization: Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt); the scan under original/<identifier>/ is the witness, and where the text layer misreads, the scan governs. Project Gutenberg transcriptions as fetched (text/<slug>.txt), with Project Gutenberg's header and licence, line endings normalized to LF; each is a transcription and is named as one beside the scan of the same edition where an open scan was found. Every Internet Archive file checked against the md5 the Archive publishes.
seats.scope: Du Bois's books to 1930, each in its first edition where an open scan was found: The Suppression of the African Slave-Trade (1896), The Philadelphia Negro (1899), The Souls of Black Folk (first edition, April 1903), John Brown (1909), The Quest of the Silver Fleece (1911), The Negro (1915), Darkwater (1920), The Gift of Black Folk (1924) and Dark Princess (1928), with Project Gutenberg transcriptions beside seven of them; The Conservation of Races (1897) and The Talented Tenth in The Negro Problem (1903), as transcriptions only; and the first number of The Crisis (November 1910), which he edited, in the facsimile of the Arno Press reprint (1969). His essay in The New Negro (1925) is seated in 26/02, with the anthology. QUEUED: the Atlanta University Publications he edited (1896–1914); The Horizon and The Moon; the further numbers of The Crisis to 1930; The Star of Ethiopia (1913); Africa, Its Place in Modern History (1930). Not seated: Black Reconstruction (1935) and everything after 1930, in copyright in the United States.

seats.why_seated: MANUS, 27 October 2026, after the twenty-seventh seating entered Deleuze and Guattari as a declared absence: "and a declared absence/ wanted seating: hypatia, d & g, pkd, allen ginsberg, anne carson, and tao lin - including the mandalas. and paul klee. too many files and too many image copyright landmines." Hypatia is entered as an absence of a different kind from the others of this seating. Her works are not held back by copyright; they are lost, or they survive inside other texts under other names. The Suda names a commentary on Diophantus, a commentary on Apollonius' Conics and an Astronomical Canon, and the heading of Theon's commentary on the third book of Ptolemy's Almagest credits the text to an edition "revised by my daughter Hypatia, the philosopher". What can be seated are the witnesses: Synesius' letters to her, the historians who record her life and death, and the texts in which her editing is believed to stand.

seats.why_seated: Jack Kerouac (1922–1969) is entered as wanted, at the operator's ruling of 2026-10-28 on the proposals of Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose: A Critical Edition (§11). His two statements of method are the model the Footnote to Pearl names (Dead Letters, #1099, post #4, 10 May 2014): "Belief & Technique for Modern Prose", thirty items, written in a letter to Donald Allen in 1958 and printed in Evergreen Review in 1959, and "Essentials of Spontaneous Prose", printed in the Black Mountain Review in 1957 and in Evergreen Review in 1958, whose word for what spontaneous prose does to its reader, "telepathic", the Footnote takes into its title. seats.scope: Arts of poetry: treatises, prefaces, letters, manifestos and poems about the making of poems, chosen for range — one or more per tradition, from the Nāṭyaśāstra and the Great Preface to the Odes through Mayakovsky, Hagiwara and MacLeish. Copyrighted moderns and contemporary arts of poetry are declared in 29/06 (ars-poetica-wanted).

seats.scope: Thirty-two works: fourteen Mahāyāna sūtras (the Lotus, the Perfection of Wisdom in 8,000 lines, the Diamond and the Heart, the Laṅkāvatāra, the Vimalakīrti, the Gaṇḍavyūha, the Samādhirāja, both Sukhāvatīvyūhas, the Kāraṇḍavyūha, the Golden Light, the Kāśyapaparivarta, the Lalitavistara); twelve śāstras (Nāgārjuna, Candrakīrti, Śāntideva, the Maitreya texts, the Ratnagotravibhāga, Vasubandhu); and six works of kāvya and narrative (Aśvaghoṣa, Āryaśūra, the Divyāvadāna, the Mahāvastu, the Udānavarga).

seats.title: The Mahāyāna in East Asia: the Chinese canon (the Lotus, the Diamond, the Heart, the Vimalakīrti), Chan from the Platform Sūtra to the Gateless Barrier, the Tannishō, Hōnen and Hakuin, and Han Yong-un's The Silence of Love
seats.edition: 《妙法蓮華經》 (the Lotus Sūtra), Kumārajīva's translation (406), twenty-eight chapters, as in the Taishō canon (T 262) — Chinese Wikisource; 《金剛般若波羅蜜經》 (the Diamond Sūtra), Kumārajīva's translation — Chinese Wikisource; 《般若波羅蜜多心經》 (the Heart Sūtra), Xuanzang's translation (649) — Chinese Wikisource; 《維摩詰所說經》 (the Vimalakīrti Sūtra), Kumārajīva's translation, fourteen chapters (T 475) — Chinese Wikisource; 《佛說阿彌陀經》 (the smaller Sukhāvatīvyūha), Kumārajīva's translation — Chinese Wikisource; seats.normalization: Wikisource pages as served under original/, each with its revision id; text/<slug>.txt the parser output reduced by code, several pages of one work joined under '=== <title> ===' headings. Nothing corrected.
seats.scope: Twenty works: nine of the Chinese canon (the Lotus in twenty-eight chapters, the Diamond, the Heart, the Vimalakīrti, the smaller Sukhāvatīvyūha, the Forty-Two Sections, the Bequeathed Teaching, the Awakening of Faith, Sengzhao); six of Chan (the Platform Sūtra, the Xinxin ming, the Zhengdao ge, the Record of Linji, the Blue Cliff Record, the Gateless Barrier); four of Japan (the Tannishō, Hōnen, Hakuin, the Heart Sūtra as read in Japan); and Korea's The Silence of Love (1926).

seats.title: The Derge Kangyur in Tibetan: the Vinaya's first volume, the Perfection of Wisdom, the sūtra volumes of the Lalitavistara, the Laṅkāvatāra, the Lotus, the Sukhāvatīvyūha and the Vimalakīrti, and the catalogue
seats.edition: The Digital Derge Kangyur of the Esukhia–Barom proofreading project (2014–2018), from the UVA–SOAS 2013 eKangyur, after the Derge woodblock edition held by the Library of Congress (BDRC W4CZ5369): Esukhia/derge-kangyur at commit a582cf471b7c85a101035071078032f106a8e536 (archived; continued as OpenPecha P000001). Eight of its 103 volumes.
